Always best if your Gerrit Name matches your CCLA / Signed-off name. Thanks!
Done
Done

- Good use of logical CSS properties throughout (inset-inline-start, inset-inline-end, margin-inline-start, padding-inline-start) — this properly supports RTL layouts.
- Removing the Vue 2 fade-enter transition class is correct cleanup, thanks!
- The auto-close="outside" addition to the filter dropdown is a good UX fix — prevents the dropdown from closing when clicking checkboxes inside it.
- Extracting previously hard-coded values into SCSS variables ($skip-link-top-offset, $nav-indicator-width, $btn-back-to-top-offset, etc.) is the right direction.
- The toast title slot approach to render StatusIcon is a creative workaround for the bootstrap-vue-next API.

This patch adds ~20+ new !important declarations. I had done the same to override Bootstrap internals, but now feel that this level of `!important` usage is a strong signal of specificity wars, and will cascade into vendor overrides.  A more sustainable approach would be auditing the CSS import order or using slightly higher specificity selectors (e.g., `body .alert` instead of `.alert`).
Removed a few of the !important declarations, and the styling still looks fine. I agree that excessive use of !important isn’t ideal, will explore a more sustainable approach
Done

This file lost the trailing newline.
POSIX standard expects files to end with a newline. 
I vote we update lint-staged in package.json to add `scss` to prettier --write:

```
    "*.{md,scss}": [
        "prettier --write"
    ]
```

Done. Restored the trailing newline in `_base.scss` and extended lint-staged so Prettier runs on `*.{md,scss}` (e.g. `\"*.{md,scss}\": [\"prettier --write\"]`), which should prevent this for SCSS and markdown going forward.
Done

consider: Bootstrap 5 already ships text-decoration-none as a utility class.
Also remove the text-decoration style from OverviewCard.vue

Removed text-decoration from OverviewCard.vue.

Agreed, since Bootstrap 5 already provides the text-decoration-none utility, I’ve removed that rule from .no-underline-link and retained only the hover styling.

The global .no-underline-link helper remains in _base.scss for existing usages (LDAP, DateTime, Inventory), so those pages are unaffected.

Added `text-decoration: none;` back under `.no-underline-link`. When using `class="text-decoration-none"`, we would otherwise need to add `text-decoration: underline !important;` for the styling to work as expected.
Done

A lot of hardcoded values here.
Values like 260px, 0.75rem, 0.25rem should either use $spacer-based calculations or be extracted to named variables for documentation and consistency.

Updated. Introduced `$table-filter-min-width: 260px`, `$table-filter-spacing: 0.75rem`, and `$table-filter-form-margin` (from `$spacer`) and replaced the previous magic numbers with these variables in the table-filter dropdown block.
Done
Conflicts with line 147 `color: $gray-600 !important;`

Resolved by making the disabled form-check label use the same token: line 131 now uses `color: $gray-600 !important;` so it matches the custom-control disabled label at line 147 and is consistent across disabled states.
Done

The selector was changed from .btn-close (Bootstrap 5) to .close (Bootstrap 4). The .close class won't match the actual close button rendered by bootstrap-vue-next, making these styles dead code. This should remain .btn-close.
Reverted to `.btn-close` so the modal header close button matches what bootstrap-vue-next renders (Bootstrap 5). The same correction was applied in _alert.scss for the alert close button.
Done

This commit adds border-radius: 0 !important in 11 separate places (buttons, cards, alerts, dropdowns, modals, toasts, pagination, forms, input groups). This is a maintenance burden and indicates the root cause isn't being addressed. If $enable-rounded: false isn't being respected, it's likely a CSS import order issue with bootstrap-vue-next — that should be investigated and fixed rather than applying !important overrides everywhere. If the variable IS working, these are all dead declarations adding noise.

Added `$border-radius: 0;` in _variables.scss so the rule is applied globally, and removed `border-radius: 0;` wherever it was specified explicitly, except where it is required to override the global rule.
Done

The `striped` prop was removed but `animated` was kept. In Bootstrap 5, the animated effect only applies to striped progress bars. Without striped, animated has no visual effect. Either remove animated too (if you don't want stripes) or restore striped (if we want to keep the animation).
IMO animation let's the user know that it is _loading..._
Removed both `striped` and `animated` from `b-progress-bar`. The loading bar remains visible, and the styling now matches the Vue2 behaviour.
Done

This hides horizontal overflow rather than fixing whatever is causing content to exceed the viewport. It can clip absolutely-positioned elements or wide tables. The root cause of any horizontal scroll should be addressed instead.

Removed `overflow-x: hidden` and fixed the root cause. Grid items default to min-width: auto, preventing shrinking below content size. Added `min-width: 0` to both PageContainer.vue and .app-content in AppLayout.vue so the container constrains content properly. Tables with responsive="md" will handle overflow with horizontal scrolling when needed.
Done

Magic number?  
Try to fix layout without using absolute.
The absolute positioning approach replaces Bootstrap's #prepend slot mechanism, which is the intended way to place icons in input groups. This is fragile across different font sizes, zoom levels, and browsers.
Removed the absolute position.
Done
Also caution against absolute here.  The clear-button also lacks explicit positioning coordinates (right/inset-inline-end), which may cause it to overlap other content.
Added `padding-inline-end: ($spacer * 2);` and `inset-inline-end: 0;` so that the clear button doesn't overlap with the search input.
Done
Typo — .dropdown-items (plural) vs .dropdown-item (singular)
Fixed: the selector is now `.filter-checkbox-labels.dropdown-item` to match Bootstrap’s `.dropdown-item` class.
Done

Adding class="b-pagination" to pagination elements suggests the component doesn't emit this class by default in bootstrap-vue-next. If so this is fine as a workaround, but should be documented as a bootstrap-vue-next compatibility shim so it can be removed if the library fixes the class emission.  Is there an issue against bootstrap-vue-next for this?  Did we try the latest version?

Done. I’ve made the required change in _pagination.scss, so the styling is now imported by default wherever the b-pagination component is used.

Removed `class="b-pagination"` wherever it was present.
Done

Duped in PostCodeLogs.vue.
Move to `_logs.scss` instead

Moved the shared log layout into `src/assets/styles/bmc/custom/_logs.scss` (imported from the bmc custom index). It defines `.margin-style` and `.logs-page.container-fluid`; EventLogs and PostCodeLogs use `class=\"logs-page\"` on their root `b-container` and no longer contain the duplicated scoped block.
Done

Since the SOL console can be launched in a standalone window (via openConsoleWindow() at line 158), it may load without the full SCSS pipeline that defines those CSS custom properties in _variables.scss. In that context, getComputedStyle would return empty strings for --sol-bg-color and --sol-accent-color, and the || fallbacks would be the only thing keeping the theme from breaking.
The fallbacks here are correct defensive coding: Please add a comment block explaining this.

Added a comment block above the getComputedStyle / SOL_THEME block explaining that the SOL console can be opened in a standalone window (openConsoleWindow()) where the full SCSS pipeline may not run, so --sol-bg-color and --sol-accent-color can be empty and the || fallbacks are necessary for the theme to still apply in that context.
Done
